question: After fixing C1 behavioral detection control to exclude 304 responses (consistent with primary metric's 304 exclusion), does C-FRESHNESS orthogonality at delta=0.15 achieve CONFIRMED status on distributed infrastructure with n_non304>=800 -- and does the C1 fix also resolve the parent audit's reporting inconsistency (C2/C7 including 304s)?
hypothesis: C-FRESHNESS orthogonality at delta=0.15 will be CONFIRMED on distributed multi-node infrastructure after fixing the C1 measurement validity issue. The parent's FALSIFIES outcome was driven entirely by 304 cache-hit responses being included in behavioral TP/TN calculation (TN=0.686 with 304s, TN=1.0 without 304s). The primary orthogonality metric (stratified pooled r=-0.0585, CI upper 0.0163 < 0.15, TOST p~0, n_non304=688) independently confirms orthogonality. Excluding 304s from C1 (consistent with the primary metric's 304 exclusion) will: (1) C1 passes (mean TN=1.0, all individual condition TN=1.0); (2) C2-C7 continue to pass (structural variance, equivalence, heterogeneity, baselines, confound all validated by parent and audit); (3) n_non304>=800 target met with additional sampling; (4) all C1-C7 PASS yields CONFIRMED status per frozen conjunctive decision rule.
falsifier: C-FRESHNESS orthogonality is REJECTED at delta=0.15 if ANY of the following occurs after the C1 304-exclusion fix: (C1) behavioral detection TP < 0.85 on distributed infrastructure (expired tokens still not detected after 304 exclusion); (C2) fewer than 2/3 endpoints have non-304 behavioral signal std > 0 OR fewer than 2/3 have non-304 structural signal std > 0; (C3) 95% CI upper bound of endpoint-stratified pooled Pearson r (non-304 samples only) >= 0.15 on distributed testbed; (C4) TOST equivalence test p_upper >= 0.05 at delta=0.15 (one-sided, endpoint-stratified non-304); (C5) endpoint-stratified cache-mode heterogeneity: |r_stratified_enabled - r_stratified_disabled| >= 2 * SE_pooled; (C6) B-LOCAL-ONLY baseline shows |r| >= 0.15 (regression from LOCAL parent); (C7) B-CONFOUND-DISTRIBUTED negative control shows endpoint-stratified weighted |r| < 0.15 (confound fails to reproduce). C-FRESHNESS orthogonality is MEASUREMENT_INVALID if infrastructure failure prevents data collection or if n_non304 < 400.

baselines.description: Single-node Flask testbed WITHOUT concurrent load or multi-node distribution -- identical to parent EXP-GRAPH-35530590140 LOCAL testbed. Re-run on same infrastructure to confirm regression-free baseline. Expected: stratified pooled r ~0.04, CI upper < 0.15.

Multi-node distributed testbed: 2 independent Flask processes on separate ports, each with independent SQLite database and in-memory CDN cache. Round-robin request routing. Each node independently generates ETag/Cache-Control headers. Cache invalidation on one node does NOT propagate to the other. Identical to parent infrastructure.

Single-node Flask testbed with 5 concurrent client sessions making simultaneous requests. Tests whether request contention, timing jitter, and interleaved cache states introduce behavioral-structural coupling. Uses gevent/threading for concurrent request generation.

Distributed negative control: same multi-node architecture as B-DISTRIBUTED but with V2 confound (fixed 'expired' request_id for expired responses, uuid4 for valid). Expected to reproduce the confound (|r| >= 0.15) across distributed nodes.
baselines.expected: |r| >= 0.15 (negative control confirming confound is genuine in distributed setting)

positive_control: Token validation failure detection on distributed infrastructure: behavioral signal must correctly identify expired vs valid tokens with TP >= 0.85 across all distributed nodes. After 304 exclusion from C1, all cache-enabled valid-token conditions that previously produced TN=0.0588 (due to 304 being treated as behavioral change) will now correctly exclude 304 responses, yielding TN=1.0 for those conditions. The testbed_server_v3.py @require_token decorator returns 401 for expired tokens and the behavioral signal extractor detects status_code, X-Token-Validation header, and session_state_change.
null_control: Structural signal std > 0 across all non-304 conditions on distributed infrastructure: independent ETag generation per node, Cache-Control headers, and UUID-based dynamic content should produce non-zero structural variation even on cache-disabled responses. Behavioral std should be non-zero on conditions with auth state variation. Same as parent -- no change required.
measurement_validity: 304 EXCLUSION FROM C1 (THE FIX): C1 behavioral detection control now excludes 304 responses from TP/TN calculation. 304 cache-hit responses are HTTP caching artifacts, not behavioral signal changes. This is consistent with the primary orthogonality metric which already excludes 304s. The fix filters 304 rows before computing C1 TP/TN.
V_ETAG_PERMISSION_LEAKAGE FIX (inherited from parent): testbed_server_v3.py decodes expired JWT tokens WITHOUT verification to extract permission_level for ETag generation.
V3 ENDPOINT-STRATIFICATION (inherited from parent): Pooled Pearson r uses endpoint-stratified weighting, not simple concatenation.
V1 UUID FOR ALL STATUS CODES (inherited from parent): All request_ids use uuid.uuid4() for all status codes in primary testbed.
304 EXCLUSION: 304 responses excluded from pooled correlation, per-endpoint correlations, per-cache correlations, AND now also from C1 behavioral detection control.
DISTRIBUTED INDEPENDENCE: Each Flask node has independent SQLite database, independent in-memory cache, independent ETag generation. No shared state between nodes.
CACHE INDEPENDENCE: Cache invalidation on node A does NOT propagate to node B. Each node CDN simulation operates independently.
ROUND-ROBIN ROUTING: Distributed testbed routes requests round-robin across nodes. Each node receives approximately equal load.
NON-304 POWER: n >= 800 non-304 samples (target: 34 per condition per endpoint x 8 conditions x 3 endpoints = 816).
TOST ONE-SIDED: C3 tests CI upper < 0.15 only; C4 tests TOST p_upper < 0.05 only (one-sided).
Testbed server must produce genuine behavioral AND structural stochastic variation on each distributed node.

Structural signal extraction uses ONLY: (a) ETag change (0/1), (b) Cache-Control change (0/1), (c) normalized Shannon entropy of UUID-based request_id, (d) SHA256(request_id)[:16] as int % 10000 / 10000.
Each endpoint must have independent behavioral and structural signal extraction -- no shared variables between signal domains.
decision_rule: C-FRESHNESS orthogonality at delta=0.15 on distributed infrastructure is CONFIRMED if ALL of: (C1) behavioral detection TP >= 0.85 across all endpoints on distributed testbed (AFTER 304 EXCLUSION); (C2) at least 2/3 endpoints have non-304 behavioral signal std > 0 AND at least 2/3 have non-304 structural signal std > 0; (C3) 95% CI upper bound of endpoint-stratified pooled Pearson r (non-304 samples only) < 0.15 on distributed testbed; (C4) TOST equivalence test p_upper < 0.05 at delta=0.15 (one-sided, non-304 samples only); (C5) endpoint-stratified cache-mode heterogeneity check (non-304 samples): |r_stratified_enabled - r_stratified_disabled| < 2 * SE_pooled; (C6) B-LOCAL-ONLY baseline shows |r| < 0.15 (no regression from parent); (C7) B-CONFOUND-DISTRIBUTED shows endpoint-stratified weighted |r| >= 0.15 (negative control passes). C-FRESHNESS orthogonality is REJECTED if ANY condition fails. MEASUREMENT_INVALID if infrastructure failure prevents data collection.
product_consequence_positive: C-FRESHNESS orthogonality confirmed on distributed production-like infrastructure. Parallel-channel architecture (separate behavioral and structural signal processing) is justified for multi-node deployment. Product may proceed with dual-signal freshness detection across distributed cache topologies.
product_consequence_negative: C-FRESHNESS orthogonality fails on distributed infrastructure even with independent caches and 304-exclusion fix. Parallel-channel architecture is NOT justified for multi-node deployment. Product must investigate cache-coupling as a correlation source and potentially use fused classifiers.
estimated_cost: Low: (1) Apply C1 304-exclusion fix to run_experiment_distributed.py ~5 lines, ~10 min; (2) Execute B-DISTRIBUTED condition ~1 hour; (3) Execute B-CONCURRENT condition ~30 min; (4) Execute B-LOCAL-ONLY baseline ~30 min; (5) Execute B-CONFOUND-DISTRIBUTED ~30 min; (6) Analysis ~30 min. Total: 2-3 compute-hours. Infrastructure reused from parent.
expected_information_gain: Very high: this is the minimum cost experiment that resolves the primary unknown from parent EXP-GRAPH-35538864957 -- whether C-FRESHNESS orthogonality achieves CONFIRMED status on distributed infrastructure. The C1 304-exclusion fix is a targeted code change (exclude 304s from TP/TN calculation) that directly addresses the sole reason for the parent's FALSIFIES outcome. The primary orthogonality metric already passes independently. A positive result (CONFIRMED) changes a product decision: parallel-channel architecture justified for multi-node deployment. A negative result (any C1-C7 fails after fix) identifies a genuine distributed infrastructure barrier. Either outcome is high-information for C-FRESHNESS claim advancement.
